articles.title: US firms laying off Americans and hiring H-1B workers to face closer scrutiny: What Trump's new order means

articles.title: Navies of India, Sri Lanka take part in bilateral maritime exercise in Visakhapatnam
articles.description: Navies of India and Sri Lanka are currently engaged in a bilateral exercise. The thirteenth edition of the Sri Lanka-India maritime exercise, SLINEX-26, is underway. This exercise aims to strengthen maritime cooperation and foster interoperability between the two nations. The event commenced with a harbour phase and will be followed by a sea phase. SLINEX-26 reinforces India's commitment to a secure and inclusive maritime environment.

articles.title: ‘NORMALIZED WAR!’: Araghchi’s BLISTERING Attack On Netanyahu | ‘How Far? Enough Is Enough!’
articles.description: Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi has launched a sharp condemnation of Israel’s actions in Gaza and what he described as the wider normalization of military force across the Middle East. Speaking virtually at the Global Townhall 2026 in Jakarta, Araghchi accused Israel and the United States of pursuing aggression and said the Gaza conflict, the war involving Iran and the destruction of civilian infrastructure reflected a broader pattern of escalating confrontation. Araghchi also raised the deaths of 168 students in Minab and questioned how long the international community would allow such conflicts to continue. He called for stronger accountability under international law and a shift away from militarism toward diplomacy, sovereignty and civilian protection.

articles.title: ‘GET OVER GREENLAND’: Residents BLAST Trump After Denmark Deal, Vow To Protect Arctic; 'Can’t Own...’
articles.description: Trump’s Greenland push has reached a new stage. After months of tensions over his demands for greater U.S. control of Greenland, Donald Trump announced a security agreement with Denmark and Greenland that he says gives Washington “permanent control” over the island’s security and other needs. The announcement has brought relief to some people in Denmark after a period of uncertainty over U.S.-Danish relations. Copenhagen and Nuuk, however, have stressed that the agreement recognizes Denmark’s sovereignty and Greenland’s right to self-determination.
